note: Plugins allowed into the Dish image. npm plugins must be pinned by version and npm tarball integrity; fetch-plugins.mjs refuses any download whose hash differs. DeepSeek is a trusted provider (Chirag, 2026-11-09): its official experimental bundles ship from the pinned upstream tree and stay off until switched on in the Plugins page. Third-party npm plugins are held: Dish runs on the naklios.dev origin, so any plugin code there can read the host's storage (web relay secret, Git token) whatever its hash; they wait for an isolated runtime (cold review, 2026-11-09).

officialLeftOut.terminal-bundle: keeps OS shell processes alive; the Worker has no OS shell
officialLeftOut.inspector-profile: its CDP hub needs node net, http and inspector
officialLeftOut.plugin-market-bundle: installs plugins at run time, which Dish does not allow
officialLeftOut.cot-translation-bundle: sends expanded reasoning to an outside translation service (Bing by default) without NakliOS consent or History

leftOut.dsh-claude-style@0.20.1: its host module uses top-level await, which the Worker's module loader refuses at pack time; it also declares dsh >=0.2.2-rc.1
leftOut.@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams@0.1.29: DeepSeek's own Agent Teams bundle covers it, and DeepSeek is a trusted provider

dsh-genui@0.3.3.reaches: system prompt; renders model-written UI in the page
dsh-genui@0.3.3.why: also loads a 6.3 MB runtime from /dsh-genui/runtime.js, an absolute path Dish's Worker does not serve, so its cards cannot render

@dfy-plugins/dsh-visualize@0.1.5.reaches: session files; renders model-written HTML in a sandboxed frame
